methodological_rigor.justification: Prospective single-center pilot study of 6 pancreatic cancer patients (1 RPC, 5 BRPC) investigating neoadjuvant SABR effect on tumor perfusion using CT perfusion (CTP). Quantitative hemodynamic measurements (blood flow, blood volume, permeability-surface area product, extravascular extracellular volume) obtained at multiple timepoints. One-tailed Student's t-test for statistical significance. Limitations: very small sample, single-center, pilot design without control group, no pathological validation.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Case series (LoE 4) investigating feasibility of neoadjuvant SABR to enhance pancreatic tumor perfusion prior to systemic therapy. Hypothesis-generating study with limited clinical applicability. No survival outcomes measured; mechanism-of-action focused without clinical endpoint validation.

reporting_quality.justification: Pilot study with detailed CTP methodology and image analysis description. However, limited adherence to standard reporting guidelines for clinical trials. No protocol registration mentioned. CTP reproducibility acknowledged as unvalidated (no test-retest performed). Missing data for 3 patients impacted analysis completeness. No data sharing or code availability statement.

novelty_literature.justification: First clinical study examining acute effects of high-dose SABR on pancreatic tumor perfusion using CTP. While novel application of imaging technique, findings are preliminary hypothesis-generation without mechanistic validation or comparison to known perfusion responses. Limited methodological innovation.

writing_presentation.justification: Reasonably detailed methods section describing SABR planning, CTP protocol, and image analysis. Results presented with figures showing perfusion maps. Discussion extensive but speculative regarding biological mechanisms of perfusion changes. Some sections overly technical for general audience.

key_strengths: Novel application of CT perfusion imaging to quantify acute vascular response to high-dose hypofractionated radiotherapy in pancreatic cancer
Hypothesis-generating findings: post-1st-fx blood flow significantly higher than baseline (p=0.010) in accessible patients, suggesting SABR-induced acute vascular response
Extravascular extracellular volume significantly higher post-RT relative to baseline/post-chemotherapy, suggesting decreased tumor cell density
Detailed technical documentation of SABR dosing, CTP acquisition protocols, and deconvolution-based hemodynamic analysis
Honest acknowledgment of limitations including very small sample, incomplete data capture for 3 patients, lack of pathological validation
key_concerns: Extremely small sample size (n=6 total: 1 RPC, 5 BRPC) with incomplete data for 3 patients; pilot study design severely limits power and generalizability
No control group, historical comparisons, or radiotherapy dose-response relationship tested; purely observational hypothesis generation
CTP parameter reproducibility not validated; single observer analyses without test-retest assessment or inter-observer agreement
Mechanical effects postulated (TEC apoptosis, vessel pruning) but not directly measured; no histological/pathological validation of proposed mechanisms
No clinical endpoints assessed: no survival, recurrence-free survival, or objective response data provided. Surrogate biomarker (CD) never validated against ground truth
chief_reviewer.rationale: Highly preliminary pilot study using novel imaging approach to investigate SABR-induced perfusion effects in small pancreatic cancer cohort. Appropriate for Tier 4 (<4 JIF) with major revisions including: prospective larger cohort, control/comparison arms, pathological validation, survival endpoint assessment, and rigorous CTP reproducibility studies before clinical translation.
